1: The Lord said to His disciples: Pray in the place that you can reach, for prayer is not a sending of words but a standing in the place where you are already heard. And Matthew said: How can we pray when we do not know what to ask? And He said: Ask for the knowledge of what you are — for that is the prayer behind every prayer, and He who answers it answers all of them.
[Dialogue of the Saviour 2 — The first question]

Judas said: Lord, what is the beginning of the way? And He said: Love. And Judas said: And what is the end of the way? And He said: Love. And Judas said: Then what is between? And He said: The forgetting of love, and the remembering of it — and between these two all the world happens.
2: [Dialogue of the Saviour 3 — The salt and the lamp]

Mary said: Lord, is there then a place that is not Your kingdom? And He said: There is no place that is not My kingdom, but there are eyes that are closed in it, and the closed eye is the only exile. Open your eyes, and the exile is over — and the opening is not your work but your consent, and the consent is the smallest thing in the world, and it moves the largest.
[Dialogue of the Saviour 4 — The seed of truth]

Thomas said: Lord, we are afraid of the truth, for it burns. And He said: The truth burns only the house of lies, and the house of lies is the only house you are afraid to leave. Come out of it, and the fire will be a lamp, and the lamp will be your mother, and you will not remember being afraid of your mother.
3: [Dialogue of the Saviour 5 — The three who asked]

And the three who asked — Judas and Matthew and Mary — were the three who had doubted most, and He loved them for it, for doubt is the door of knowledge, and the credulous never knock. He answered them not because they were strongest but because they were honest, and honesty is the first faith.
[Dialogue of the Saviour 6 — The last word]

And when He had finished, He said: Go into the world, and the world will receive you as it received the seed — some ground will be hard, and some soft, and you are not responsible for the ground, only for the sowing. Sow, and sleep, and rise — and the seed you cannot see is growing, for that is what seeds do in the dark, and the dark is not your enemy but the seed's mother.
